Our Environment Doesnt Respond To Miles Per Gallon It Responds To Gallons

Aug 1, 2009 • Janice Cotcher

That is the technical goal of efficiency; but that is not how it translates into action. When the efficiency of the 1950’s automobile was achieved people found themselves able to drive on long family vacations, to live further away from work, to do so much more and consume so many more gallons with their newer, more efficient cars.

Efficiency makes that second car more affordable, that more distant vacation costs fewer dollars to drive to. Efficiency will not translate into fewer gallons used unless attitudes and habits are changed in tandem.

To reduce environmental damage, increasing efficiency isn’t the only or primary concern. Increasing efficiency will only decrease gallons if all other considerations remain the same. If people use more cars or drive further, then gallons will not necessarily decrease. In other words, “the most efficient car you can drive is the one that you don’t drive.”
